steps.content: The next day, you compile everything Cassian mentioned during the interrogation into a detailed report. After reading it through, word by word, he finally nods and agrees to go with you.
You soon arrive at the department in charge and go through the procedures: submitting the materials, meeting with the officers, confirming your petition, and giving testimony.
The process is cold, but efficient enough. Once everything is done, you let out a long sigh of relief and stretch your stiff shoulders.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Phew... finally done. Now we just wait for their investigation and follow-up. How are you holding up?
You smile at Cassian, and he turns to meet your gaze, his lips curved up.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: I'm alright, thanks to you.
But in that same moment, his gaze freezes.
You notice his expression change. Following his line of sight, you spot a well-dressed young man strolling down the hallway.
The moment his eyes meet Cassian's, the young man stops. A flash of surprise crosses his face, quickly replaced by a gentle, yet inscrutable, smile.

steps.speaker: Young Noble
steps.content: ...Ah. I never thought I'd see you here.
He walks toward you, his voice calm yet tinged with patronizing regret, like he's commenting on an old trinket gathering dust for too long.

steps.speaker: Young Noble
steps.content: You've changed. Even your eyes aren't the same. You used to look at us so cautiously, as if terrified that one wrong move would get you thrown out.
You feel Cassian tense beside you imperceptibly. He says nothing, eyes downcast, reining in some roiling emotion.

steps.speaker: Young Noble
steps.content: It's a good thing.
For a split second, you notice the whiteness of Cassian's knuckles and sense a kind of bewilderment—not anger, but a much deeper-seated weariness.
He has achieved his long-sought revenge, and he is no longer the child desperate for acceptance. But in doing so, he's lost his purpose, uncertain what he's even living for now.
The young noble finally glances your way, his eyes sweeping over you as if you're an insignificant prop on a stage.

steps.speaker: Young Noble
steps.content: A new friend?

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: This is ${PlayerName}, Chief of the MBCC.
The young noble is taken aback, and his expression becomes guarded and complex. His smile softens, however, now laced with a veiled probing and mockery, like a blade in the water.

steps.speaker: Young Noble
steps.content: I see. You always were... good at choosing the right people to keep close. In that sense, you haven't changed much at all.
He turns to you, his tone taking on a gentlemanly warmth.

steps.speaker: Young Noble
steps.content: It's a pleasure to make your acquaintance, esteemed Chief from the Bureau. I hear you've been terribly busy lately. We appreciate your hard work.
His tone is proper, his attitude civil, but his eyes scan you with unconcealed appraisal, trying to judge whether you are worthy of his courtesy.
Though you find this pompous youth rather distasteful, you're compelled to give a slight nod out of politeness. He doesn't seem to care, just smiles before steering the conversation back to Cassian.

steps.speaker: Young Noble
steps.content: He was always like this, you know. Always knew how to make people "like" him. Especially when he needed something from you.
He says it nonchalantly, with the air of someone reminiscing about a harmless past, yet every word is meant to pick at old wounds.

steps.speaker: Young Noble
steps.content: In our circles, he was always... quite the likable figure. Docile, proper, understanding, never stepping out of line. He always smiled at the right moment and said the right words, just like...
He pauses, his smile deepening. His voice is light as a feather, but carries the hidden prick of a thorn.

steps.speaker: Young Noble
steps.content: Like he was carefully tamed.

steps.speaker: Young Noble
steps.content: Back then...
Cassian was still a boy when his life veered off course.

His father, a low-level clerk, happened to meet Falke, an influential official from Eastside, during a government function. Unexpectedly catching Falke's eye, he was quickly promoted, his career soaring and his family rising with him.
From then on, Cassian's family was no longer obscure. They were catapulted into Eastside's political scene, the "lucky newcomers" in the spotlight of high society.

The family was swept into that world, and Cassian was quickly transferred to an academy for nobles, where he took classes, dined, and attended festivals and balls with peers who were born with silver spoons in their mouths.
But Cassian and his family knew that simply entering that world was not enough. Truly securing their footing would be the real struggle they had to endure.

steps.speaker: Father
steps.content: Cassian. I know this will be exhausting and hard to accept. But I need you to understand that we are different from the other families.

steps.speaker: Father
steps.content: We're ordinary people who stumbled into fortune. But at the end of the day, we're not one of them, and perhaps we never can be...

steps.speaker: Father
steps.content: The things we fight tooth and nail for are things they get without lifting a finger. So you must always be mindful of your words and actions. Be humble and polite to everyone. That's the only way you won't give them a reason to find fault.

steps.speaker: Father
steps.content: You must always appreciate what we have now. Know that this is all due to luck, and just preserving it will be difficult enough.
Cassian, of course, understood. The precocious boy had seen the arrogance and recklessness of his peers, yet never once thought to imitate them.
He knew that he was not one of them. Only by treading carefully could he carve out a small space for himself in the margins of their world.
Beyond earning excellent grades every year, he had put in so much more effort: dining etiquette, art appreciation, ballroom dancing, golf, wine tasting, musical instruments...
He mastered every skill associated with the upper class. To be worthy of his new status, he applied himself diligently to everything, never daring to slack off.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: Darling, you're too hard on yourself. Let yourself relax, please?

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: Don't worry, Mom. I know what I'm doing.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: I'm not being hard on myself. I'm learning to become the person I need to be. Maybe when I fit in, I can make true friends.
That was how Cassian reassured his mother.
But he knew it was a mere fantasy. Those people never had any intention of accepting him. He would always be standing on the wrong side of the door.
Even so, he had to keep going.

steps.speaker: Classmate A
steps.content: Cassian's quite pretty, isn't he? I heard Miss Carr from the other class wants him to be her boyfriend. She's been sending him afternoon tea treats.

steps.speaker: Classmate B
steps.content: Really? That Miss Carr who goes through boyfriends like tissues? You know how she likes to pick her playthings from among the commoners. She'll get bored and toss him aside. Doesn't that mean... hee hee.

steps.speaker: Teacher A
steps.content: Cassian is a sensible boy who knows his place. He does whatever I ask without a mistake, which is wonderful. Having such an obedient student who's at your beck and call makes our lives so much easier.

steps.speaker: Teacher B
steps.content: His grades are exceptional, but you know... grades alone are worthless here.

steps.speaker: Councilor A
steps.content: Their son? Of course we know him. He has the most beautiful hands. It's a pleasure to watch them, whether he's playing the piano or mixing a drink.

steps.speaker: Councilor B
steps.content: To be fair, the boy is certainly talented. He works hard, and he's better than most. But you know Falke. He didn't promote that family out of some laughable "appreciation." It's best to keep your distance.

steps.speaker: Councilor A
steps.content: Tsk, tsk. What a shame.
The teasing remarks came disguised as compliments, but Cassian keenly sensed that in their eyes, he was nothing more than a novel, entertaining object.
The mockery in their tone, the relish in their eyes, the perverse amusement... they never felt the need to hide them.

steps.speaker: Classmate A
steps.content: Cassian used to be a commoner. He lived on that street on the west end of Eastside. What kind of street is that? I don't know... Ugh, of course I've never been to a place like that. I never would.

steps.speaker: Classmate B
steps.content: Cassian, I hear you play the piano well. My father's pianist fell ill. Why don't you take his place and perform for our dinner party? Don't keep everyone waiting.

steps.speaker: Elite A
steps.content: The way you hold your glass is quite convincing! A pity it's just an imitation. True elegance comes from one's breeding, and you... ah, sadly, you weren't born with it.

steps.speaker: Elite B
steps.content: My dear, we don't really need your opinion. You're pretty enough that just standing here is your ticket in. So promise me you won't think too hard, alright? A beautiful vase doesn't need to think. Neither do you.
Faced with such blatant mockery, such malicious scrutiny, Cassian maintained his composure and never dropped his pleasant smile. Yet only he knew that his heart was already scarred by fractures.
Swallow all the contempt and humiliation. Endure all the prejudice and cold stares. This is life. Grind up the pain, force it down your throat, and smile.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: Even if they never thought of me as one of them.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: Even if they never planned on leaving a corner for me to stand in.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: Even if we will never, ever exist in the same world.

...But what does it matter? His father was still trying to master the art of socializing he was so bad at. His mother was hosting every dinner with anxious care. His aunts and uncles were exhausted with pleasantries at tea parties, forcing themselves to keep up a facade of grace.
Cassian couldn't turn a blind eye to the efforts of his family, and he must do the same: he must endure, ignore the malice, and keep climbing.
He couldn't allow himself to stop. He couldn't allow himself to fall.
So he learned to be numb, forgot how to feel pain, and abandoned himself. He became a weightless shadow, existing only for his family and their "honor."
As the shadows of the past fade away, the face of the man before him overlaps with memories that feel like they belong to another lifetime. For a moment, it all seems absurdly comical.
After everything he's been through, Cassian is no longer the same person he once was.
He looks coolly at this "old friend." Even from the sofa, looking up, Cassian keeps his back straight. He unclenches his fist, and a sardonic smile slowly spreads across his lips.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: After all these years, you haven't changed at all. But I don't need to be your dog anymore.
His voice is calm, but his words are sharp as blades. The man freezes, as if he didn't understand.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: So stop clinging to the past. You're not a child anymore, still obsessing over who climbed up from where. It just sounds... pathetic.

The words aren't loud or heated, but they land squarely on the man's pride like a dull blow. This is the first time Cassian has ever, in the light of day, returned the spite he was given. He will no longer tolerate their malice. He will no longer stay silent.
It's true, he has nothing now. But it also means he no longer has to live at their mercy.
The young noble's face darkens. He opens his mouth as if to argue, but fumbles for words. His eyes dart around for a moment before landing back on you, and he forces a strained smile.

steps.speaker: Young Noble
steps.content: Heh. You talk tough now that you've found a new master.

steps.speaker: Young Noble
steps.content: But you're still the same, always climbing up on someone else's back. Don't say I didn't warn you. You should remember very well... how you got in, and how you came crashing down.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Rest assured, we both have excellent memories. But some things won't be happening again.
You raise an eyebrow at the young noble and cut in coldly, your tone official and direct.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: He is now a consulting investigator for the MBCC and a key figure in our ongoing case concerning Eastside elites.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Given the current climate, I'm sure a man as smart and respectable as yourself understands that some people are no longer yours to order around.

He glares at you, his face pale. You can see he desperately wants to fire back, but is likely deterred by your title as Chief of the MBCC. Swallowing his anger, the young noble forces out a "Fine, fine," and beats a hasty, undignified retreat.
You spread your hands and give Cassian an innocent shrug.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Was it something I said? Why'd he get so worked up?
Cassian looks down and chuckles softly, shaking his head. There's a resigned look in his eyes.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: I'm sorry. I put you in a difficult position.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Not at all. I was just telling the truth.
You pause, your voice firm and sincere.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Cassian, I've never once thought you needed to depend on anyone. Even if you once forgot who you were, you should know by now—you are not, and never have been, anyone's accessory.
He looks up at you, and for a second, you see a flicker disturb the calm of his eyes, like ripples on still water.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: You've always been yourself.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Since we're already here, why don't we stop by and see someone?
When you suggest visiting his "uncle" at Eastside Prison, Cassian's expression changes. For a moment, he says nothing.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: I'm not going.
His voice is low and final, a gut reaction. He abruptly stops walking, his shoulders tense.
You stop too and look at him, confused.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: From what I've heard, he isn't one of your relatives, but you were close. He worked with your family for years. Were you not on good terms?

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: No. We were. That's why I...
Cassian smiles bitterly and avoids your gaze.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: He was my father's best friend. He watched me grow up, and I... I haven't seen him in years.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: During that conspiracy, my family knew they were doomed. But they fought with their last breath to save my life.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: Uncle helped me so much... but he ended up in prison because of us. I dragged him down with me. And now I've ended up like this. How am I supposed to face him?
His fingers instinctively drift to the scar on his cheek before falling back to his side.
You look at him and let out a soft sigh.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: But he deserves to hear the good news. And you're the only one who has the right to deliver it. Isn't that right?
Cassian falls silent. He wants to object, but can't find the strength. Something tightens in his throat, making it hard to breathe.
In the end, he goes with you.

The prison visiting room is stark and silent. Cassian sits on one side of the transparent partition, his head bowed, though his back is ramrod straight. His face looks even more haggard in the bleak gray light.
His fingertips dig into his knees, as if clinging to his last line of retreat.
He stiffens when the door is pushed open.

The heavy iron door creaks open. The footsteps that enter are slow, but as steady as they've always been. The man is dressed in a prison uniform. His face is weathered and his black hair streaked with gray, but he still carries himself with a hint of his old dignity.
Cassian recognizes him instantly. At the same moment, the man he's always known as his uncle sees him.
Time seems to stop. Cassian's heart hammers against his ribs, his breath catching in his chest.
He hangs his head awkwardly, unable to meet the man's eyes, trying to hide the scar on his face with his hair. He tucks his hands behind his back, anxiously twisting the hem of his shirt.
He's afraid.
Afraid of being blamed. Afraid of seeing disappointment. Afraid of being asked: we gave everything to save you, why did you turn out this way?
But the man seems lost for words.
He slowly approaches the partition. From a pocket close to his chest, he carefully removes a yellowed photograph.
It's an old photo of him with Cassian's family. The image is worn from being touched over and over, its corners curled, the creases nearly torn.
He gazes at the picture for a long while before finally looking up at Cassian, his eyes gentle in a way that seems impossible for someone imprisoned for years.
A smile slowly spreads across his face. He raises a hand to his own shoulder.

steps.speaker: Uncle
steps.content: You've grown up.

steps.speaker: Uncle
steps.content: The last time I saw you, you were only... about this tall.
At those words, Cassian jerks his head up, his eyes wide with bewilderment. His throat feels tight, his chest heaving.
No blame.
No criticism of his failure, no questions about why he had taken so long, not even the slightest trace of resentment.
Just that simple, almost clumsy phrase: "You've grown up." As if all these years, he hadn't been waiting for vindication or release. He was only waiting to know that this child was still alive.
Cassian stares at him, stunned.

He sees how much has changed in this man, his father's closest friend, who used to clap him on the shoulder and say with a laugh, "Your dad was even more of a troublemaker than you back then." Gone is his former vigor. His shoulders are thin, his eyes wrinkled at the corners, his lips pale and chapped. Even his voice is raspy.
And still, he smiles.
As if nothing has changed, as if time hasn't taken anything away. As if he's still standing at the door, waiting for Cassian to come home from school.
Suddenly, Cassian can't breathe.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: Sorry...
His voice is choked and broken, almost like his throat is run through with rusty nails.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: I... couldn't protect anything.
He covers his face, the metal of the finger brace pressed against his scar. The wound feels raw again, the pain churning through his flesh.
Watching his shoulders tremble, you finally understand.

He has never been unfeeling. He simply buries all his pain in silence, tucks it away inside the brooch he keeps in his pocket but never wears, hides it in the finger brace he cannot remove and the past he dares not touch.
And in this moment, he finally allows himself to cry.
The older man raises his shackled hands and gently presses them to the visitor's window. His rough, dry fingers are covered in tiny cracks, but they're still warm.

steps.speaker: Uncle
steps.content: You're alive.
He says softly.

steps.speaker: Uncle
steps.content: You're here before me. That alone... is enough.
The visitation time is over, and Cassian watches his uncle disappear behind the door. He follows you in a daze, bumping into people without seeming to notice.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: The paperwork is in. Once Falke's crimes are made public, your uncle's exoneration will be processed immediately.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: You'll be able to bring him home soon. You two can finally start a proper life together.

It's a beautiful day. The sun is shining, and the chattering of birds seems to rouse every slumbering soul. The streets are bustling with crowds and traffic; even the car horns sound unusually cheerful and alive.
For the first time, it dawns on Cassian:
Perhaps the past isn't beyond repair.
Maybe... he could rebuild connections. Earn the right to live. Be accepted by the world again.
Out of habit, Cassian reaches into his pocket to touch the family brooch he always carries with him. It's what he does whenever he needs strength.
This time, his fingers stop short.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Cassian? What's wrong?
Noticing his pause, you stop and turn to him. Under the bright sun, his face has gone deathly pale.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: My brooch. It's gone.
